key_insight: Short-lived, recurrent EEG microstates can be used as compact, interpretable "atoms" of brain activity to learn universal, transferable EEG representations that generalize across tasks and subjects.
problem_solved: How to obtain compact, task-agnostic EEG representations that are interpretable, robust to noise and inter-subject variability, and suitable for transfer across downstream BCI and neuroimaging tasks.
method: Segment raw EEG into microstates (recurrent scalp topographies) and extract discrete sequence features (labels, durations, transitions, occurrence frequencies).
Train a task-agnostic encoder on microstate-derived features using self-/task-agnostic objectives to produce low-dimensional, universal EEG embeddings.
Demonstrate that these microstate-based embeddings transfer effectively to downstream tasks (e.g., classification, decoding) while being more compact and interpretable than raw/time-frequency inputs.
impact: Provides ML practitioners a lightweight, interpretable representation for EEG that improves sample-efficiency and cross-task/subject transfer, simplifying model design for BCIs and clinical EEG applications.
visual_elements: Scalp topography icons showing a small set of learned microstate prototypes (color-coded maps).
Timeline of EEG with segmented microstate labels and durations (showing how continuous signal maps to discrete atoms).
Embedding scatter (UMAP/t-SNE) visualizing cluster separation of microstate-derived representations across tasks/conditions.
Pipeline diagram: EEG → microstate extraction → encoder → universal embeddings → downstream tasks (classification/transfer).
paper_title: Atoms of Thought: Universal EEG Representation Learning with Microstates
paper_authors: Xinyang Tian, Ruitao Liu, Ziyi Ye, Siyang Xue, Xin Wang
